title: Spatiotemporal multiomics uncover tumor ecosystem dynamics during metastatic colonization.
data_url: https://db.cngb.org/stomics/datasets/STDS0000387/ (mouse Stereo-seq, browse only); CNSA project CNP0005341; human scRNA-seq OMIX005812 (controlled access)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: I opened every repository page the paper points to. STOmicsDB dataset STDS0000387 (the mouse spatial atlas) lists 26 processed AnnData files (.h5ad, e.g. T1_M01_section1.h5ad) across 18 samples and 9 time points, but the page's own file records say download=false and file_size='unsized', i.e. browse/visualise only. The China National GeneBank Sequence Archive (CNSA) project CNP0005341 has no directory under any public FTP folder (I listed /pub/CNSA/data1 through data7; neighbouring projects CNP0005350 and CNP0005359 are there, CNP0005341 is not). The human single-cell RNA sequencing set OMIX005812 lists 9 expression-matrix zips (5.2-120.9 MB) but is labelled 'Controlled-access' with a 'Request for this Data' button. The GitHub code repository liushang17/Lung_Metastasis contains 21 R scripts totalling ~47 KB and no data and no licence. Europe PMC shows no open full text, no supplementary files; NCBI elink from PubMed 42531396 returns no GEO, SRA or BioProject records; a Zenodo search on the DOI returns nothing.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the biology (quiescent Phgdh-high disseminated tumour cells, CX3CR1-high interstitial macrophages, H3K27me3-mediated chemokine silencing) comes from the abstract and the repository summary, since the Science full text is paywalled and not in PubMed Central. Cell counts, spot counts and gene counts are unknown: the STOmicsDB record reports cells=0, spots=0, genes=0, so no row count was verified anywhere.

a1_downloadable.note: No anonymous download exists. Mouse processed Stereo-seq files are flagged download=false in STOmicsDB (visualisation only); CNSA project CNP0005341 is absent from all seven public CNSA FTP folders; the human single-cell data (OMIX005812, BioProject PRJCA023486) is explicitly controlled-access and needs a data request. Checked on the repository pages, not inferred from the paper.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked because no file could be opened. Time point after injection (T1 0.25 h to T9 35 days) is sample-level metadata and would be a clean label if the files were released; a cell-level label such as 'quiescent Phgdh-high disseminated tumour cell' would have to be reconstructed from the authors' clustering, which lives in R scripts, not in a table.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked. The inputs would be spatial coordinates plus gene counts inside each .h5ad file, which is the right format, but no file is retrievable.

a4_units_stated.note: Not checked. Stereo-seq counts are unique-molecule counts per spatial bin, normally stated inside the AnnData object, but the object is not downloadable.

a5_enough_rows.note: No row count verified. The repository reports 18 samples and 26 tissue sections across 9 time points and lists cells=0, spots=0, genes=0 (placeholders), so the number of cells or spatial bins is unknown.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; 26 Stereo-seq sections at single-cell bin size would plausibly be tens of GB, but every file is listed as 'unsized'
a6_fits_laptop.note: Not assessable: no file sizes are published for the mouse data and nothing could be downloaded to measure.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable. Abstract and repository agree qualitatively (nine time points, mouse lung metastasis), but no numeric count exists in both places to compare.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not checked. Time point would be a true experimental variable (good provenance), but the paper's headline cell states are outputs of the authors' own clustering and annotation pipeline, which is a model-derived label and would need care.

existing_models.name: Nicheformer (a transformer pretrained on single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; named in a 2025/2026 review of spatial transcriptomics foundation models as doing spatial label identification, composition deconvolution and neighbourhood-density prediction after fine-tuning.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved (I only saw it described in a secondary review, not its own paper).

existing_models.name: CellPLM (a cell language model that encodes spatial coordinates as positional information)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; described in the same review as handling cell-type annotation, perturbation prediction and spatial imputation.

backbone.name: Nicheformer or CellPLM (spatial single-cell foundation models); scGPT/Geneformer for the dissociated single-cell part
backbone.hardware: Embedding a few hundred thousand cells on a 16 GB CPU laptop is slow but feasible in batches; fine-tuning would need a GPU.
backbone.licence: Not checked, because the biological data this would be applied to is not obtainable.

integration.partner_dataset: Tabula Muris Senis / mouse lung single-cell references and the mouse Stereo-seq ten-organ atlas, joinable on mouse gene symbols or Ensembl mouse gene IDs
integration.join_key: Ensembl mouse gene ID / MGI gene symbol
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does the local cellular neighbourhood around a single disseminated tumour cell predict whether that cell will be cleared, stay dormant, or expand into a metastasis? - unanswerable here because the measurements are not released.

controls.positive_control: Would have been: recover the known rise in Phgdh expression and the drop in chemokine expression in tumour cells between early and late time points, which the paper reports.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle time-point labels across tissue sections and confirm performance falls to the majority-class baseline.
controls.external_validation: The human hepatocellular carcinoma lung metastasis single-cell data (OMIX005812) would have been the external set, but it is controlled-access.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the only honest statement is that a model trained on the mouse lung sections would describe one cell line (Hepa 1-6) injected intravenously into male C57BL/6J mice, and even that cannot be attempted because neither the mouse nor the human matrices can be downloaded.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the cells surrounding a single spread tumour cell in lung tissue to predict how far metastasis has progressed.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one disseminated tumour cell plus the gene expression of its spatial neighbourhood, taken from 26 mouse lung sections measured by Stereo-seq (a spatial gene-expression method). The number of cells is unknown; the repository lists cells=0 as a placeholder.
plain_idea.predict: The time point after tumour-cell injection (0.25 hours to 35 days, nine levels), or whether the surrounding tissue is the immune-scarce niche the paper describes. The true answer comes from the experiment's own design (when the lung was harvested), which is solid provenance.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups studying dormant metastatic cells would get a way to read 'stage of colonisation' off a tissue section, and a negative result would still say that neighbourhood composition alone cannot time metastatic progression.

more_or_better_data.why: A nine-time-point spatial time course from 0.25 hours to 35 days is genuinely unusual, but we cannot obtain a single byte of it, so there is no data advantage to claim.

confidence_score.why: Replicate structure (two sections per sample for some mice) exists on paper and would support a noise estimate, but the files are not downloadable, so nothing can be computed.

models_beatable.why: Spatial foundation models such as Nicheformer and CellPLM are recent and open, so beating them is not easy; but no model has been fitted to this particular colonisation time course.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The first condition fails outright: we cannot run any baseline on this data because the data cannot be retrieved.

ml_idea: Predict the stage of metastatic colonisation (nine harvest time points from 0.25 hours to 35 days) from the spatial gene-expression neighbourhood around each disseminated tumour cell in mouse lung Stereo-seq sections, then test whether the learned niche signature transfers to human hepatocellular carcinoma lung metastases. Not attemptable: neither the mouse spatial files nor the human single-cell matrices can be downloaded.

effort.compute_note: No estimate possible: every mouse file is listed as 'unsized' in STOmicsDB and nothing could be downloaded to measure. Only the human controlled-access zips have stated sizes (5.2-120.9 MB each, 9 files).
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the STOmicsDB file table and read the 'download' flag - it is false for all 26 mouse files - then grep the public CNSA FTP listings for CNP0005341, which returns nothing. Both took under five minutes and kill the project.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails. The mouse spatial files are visualisation-only in STOmicsDB (download disabled, no sizes), the CNSA project CNP0005341 is absent from every public FTP folder, and the human single-cell data is controlled-access requiring a formal request; the only open artefact is 47 KB of R plotting scripts.
